# Danmarks Statistik

Danmarks Statistik is Denmark's national statistical authority. In the context of this corpus, it appears as the data source underpinning an educational-outcomes indicator within the ADHD-databasen, a Danish health database that monitors the quality of diagnosis and treatment of ADHD in children and young people under 18 [^src1][^src2]. Specifically, data on the folkeskole leaving examination (folkeskolens afgangsprøve) is drawn from Danmarks Statistik [^src1], and the database's documentation states that "Indikatoren er baseret på data fra Danmarks Statistik. Datakompletheden er således god da alle eksamensresultater fra folkeskoler i Danmark registreres" [^src2] — meaning the indicator's data completeness is considered good because all examination results from Danish primary and lower-secondary schools are registered.

This role places Danmarks Statistik at the center of one of the ADHD-databasen's most striking findings: children and young people with ADHD have a markedly lower rate of passing the folkeskole leaving exam before age 17 compared with the background population. According to the broader chunk context surrounding these mentions, the database's reporting for the period 01.04.2024–31.03.2025 found that only 53% of the assessment ("udredning") population had passed the exam, versus 84% in the background population — a gap that relies on the exam-result data Danmarks Statistik supplies. The same reporting period also covered medication-use indicators, sourced separately from the lægemiddelstatistikdatabasen, alongside the Danmarks Statistik-derived education figures, together supporting the database's claim of high data completeness.

Danmarks Statistik itself is not otherwise profiled in the corpus beyond its function as a data provider; no organizational history, leadership, or independent relationships are documented here. Its significance in this wiki is narrowly but clearly defined: it is the authoritative registry from which the ADHD-databasen draws nationwide, near-complete exam-result data used to measure educational outcomes for children and young people with ADHD [^src1][^src2].
